card_title: The 5 ChatGPT Settings I'd Change First
card_desc: One you need to turn OFF, and four to turn on. What each one does and where to find it.
meta_title: 5 ChatGPT Settings to Change Today (and Where to Find Them) | Olivia Porter
meta_description: The 5 ChatGPT settings I'd change first: turn OFF model training on your chats, then turn on custom instructions, memory, multi-factor authentication, and connected apps.
sub: One to turn OFF, four to turn on. Click your name, then Settings.
intro: Here are the 5 ChatGPT settings I'd change. Four you turn on. One you turn OFF, and that one matters most, so it's first.

sections.label: Turn this OFF
sections.title: Stop ChatGPT training on your chats

steps.title: Improve the model for everyone: OFF
steps.text: Settings > Data controls > Improve the model for everyone. Switch it off. Yes, this still matters: on Free, Plus and Pro accounts it's on by default, which lets OpenAI use your chats, and anything your connected apps pull in, to train its models.
list: ChatGPT Business, Enterprise and Edu workspaces aren't used for training by default.
Using Claude? Same idea. On Free, Pro and Max plans, go to Settings > Privacy and turn off the option that lets your chats be used to train models.

steps.title: Custom instructions
steps.text: Personalization > Custom instructions. Tell it who you are, what you sell, who your clients are, and how you write. I also tell it never to use em dashes.

steps.title: Memory
steps.text: Personalization > Memory. Turn it on, so you stop repeating yourself.

steps.title: Multi-factor authentication
steps.text: Security > Multi-factor authentication. Turn it on.

steps.title: Connected apps
steps.text: Settings > Plugins (you may see it called Apps or Connectors). Connect Google Drive and your calendar so it can work with your real files. Turn training off first, so what it reads stays out of training.

closing: Menu names move around sometimes. If you can't find one, search for it in Settings.
